items.text: A Japanese woman born at the dawn of the 20 th century has died at the age of 119. Kane Tanaka was born on January 2, 1903, and she died on April 19. At the age of 19, Tanaka married a rice shop owner, and she worked in the family store until she was 103. She twice survived cancer, and she lived through a multitude of historical events. She survived two world wars, the 1918 Spanish flu, and the COVID-19 pandemic. Tanaka had been living in a nursing home in Fukuoka, and according to her family, she kept her mind and body engaged by doing math and remaining curious. According to 2020 data, one in every 1,565 people in Japan was over 100 years old. More than 88% of them were women. Government numbers released in July 2020 showed that women had a life expectancy of 87.45 years compared to 81.4 years for men. Difficult words: multitude (a large number of people or things), nursing home (a private institution that provides a home and healthcare to elderly people), life expectancy (the number of years a person can expect to live). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The oldest woman in the world died on April 19 at the age of 119. Kane Tanaka was born in Japan in 1903. When she was 19, she married an owner of a rice shop. She worked there until she was 103. For the past few years, Tanaka lived in a nursing home in the city of Fukoka. Many historical events happened during her life. The woman lived through both world wars, the 1918 Spanish flu, and the COVID-19 pandemic. Also, she survived cancer twice. In 2020, one in every 1,565 people in Japan was more than 100 years old, and 88% of them were women. Women’s life expectancy was 87.45 years, and men’s life expectancy was 81.4 years. Difficult words: nursing home (a place where elderly people live), cancer (a disease when a part of the body starts to grow without control), life expectacy (the number of years which a person can expect to live). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Kane Tanaka is the oldest woman in the world. She is 119 years old. She dies on April 19. Tanaka lives in the city of Fukoka, Japan. She marries an owner of a shop when she is 19 years old. Tanaka works in the shop until she is 103. The woman spends the last years of her life in a nursing home. A nursing home is a place where elderly people live. Tanaka likes math. She likes to learn new things. Her family says that these things help her live so long. Tanaka is born in 1903. She lives through both world wars. She survives the Spanish flu pandemic in 1918. She survives COVID-19, too. Difficult words: owner (a person who has something, and it belongs to him), elderly (old), survive (to live after something bad happens). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People made a discovery during restoration work at one of Peru’s earliest Christian sites, the Saint Francis of Assisi Temple. Buried deep inside this centuries-old crypt that archaeologists accidentally stumbled upon, are human bones that could total up to 32 complete skeletons. The remains are in bad condition after hundreds of years’ worth of disturbances at the site. Archaeologists say that the crypt, which is thought to be more than 500 years old, was used as a burial site for early believers. A mural of the Christian nativity scene , which people believe is part of the original decoration at the temple, was also found. Difficult words: stumble (find something by chance), disturbance (activity), mural (a painting on a wall), nativity scene (a model which represents the birth of Jesus Christ). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People made a discovery during restoration work of a temple in Peru. The temple is one of the country’s oldest Christian sites. By accident, scientists found a 500 year-old crypt with bones from 32 people. The bones are in bad condition. The scientists also found a painting on a wall of the Christian nativity scene . Difficult words: restoration (making something old nice again), temple (a building that is like a church), crypt (dead people stay in this underground room), nativity scene (a model which represents the birth of Jesus Christ). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is from Peru. Experts work on a church. It is a very old church. They want to make it nice again. During the work, they find something. It is a crypt . It is 500 years old. There are bones inside the crypt. They are human bones. These bones are from 32 people. Experts also find a painting. It is a painting on a wall. It shows baby Jesus. Difficult words: during (when), crypt (an underground room for dead people), bone (the hard white material in your body). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A driver and a passenger had a lucky escape when a taxi rolled over in the middle of a busy street in China. A security camera filmed the moment that the car overturned, as the left front wheel collided with the pillar in the middle of the road. The taxi driver said that he did not notice the pillar that he had crashed into. Passer-by rushed to help the taxi driver and the passenger from the car once it overturned. Difficult words: collide (crash into), pillar (a pole used for guiding cars), passer-by (a person who is passing by when something happens). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A Chinese taxi driver was turning left at a crossroads . He didn’t notice a pillar and drove into it with the front left wheel. It turned the taxi over. The crash did not hurt the taxi driver and his passenger, and people quickly came to the taxi to help them. The crash broke the windshield and side mirrors of the car. Police say that the taxi driver wasn’t looking out when he turned left. Difficult words: crossroads (a place where roads meet), pillar (a pole used for guiding cars where to drive), look out (to be careful and look). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Here is news from China. A taxi driver is at a crossroads . He turns left. He isn’t careful. He does not see a pillar . He drives into it. His car turns over. The crash damages the car. The crash injures nobody. People see the accident. They come to the car and help the man. Difficult words: crossroads (a place where more roads meet), pillar (a thing to show cars where to drive), damage (to break). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Twitter agreed to sell a 44-billion deal to Tesla CEO Elon Musk; the deal ends the social media platform’s time as a public company. Twitter has millions of users and global leaders, and the transaction shifts control to the world’s richest man. The company resisted the billionaire’s takeover , but it changed course after Musk unveiled a financial package. It included 33.5 billion dollars from his own fortune. Musk is an active Twitter user, and he has more than 83 million followers. In the past, he said that Twitter needed to be private to grow and become a genuine platform for free speech. After news of the sale, people called on Musk to return access to the social media platform to former US president Donald Trump. Difficult words: takeover (when a company buys another company and gets control), unveil (to show publicly for the first time), genuine (truly what something is said to be). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Elon Musk is the world’s richest man; he announced that he was buying Twitter. Since 2013, Twitter was a public company , and now, it will become private . Millions of people use Twitter, and world leaders also use it. Twitter banned the previous US president Donald Trump, and now, some people expect that Trump will return. In the past, Musk said that Twitter needed to change, and the only possible way to do it was to make it a private company. The change was important for freedom of speech on Twitter. At first, the company didn’t want Musk to buy it, but his offer interested them. He offered to buy Twitter for 44 billion dollars, and 33.5 billion of those dollars were his money. Difficult words: public company (a company which sold all or a part to the public), private (something that only belongs to one person or a group of people), freedom of speech (the right that anyone can freely say what he thinks). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Elon Musk is the richest man in the world. He buys Twitter. Twitter is a public company since 2013. Public means that anyone can buy a part of the company. Musk says that this is not good. Twitter must be private . Millions of people use Twitter. World leaders and other important people use it. Twitter bans the previous US president Donald Trump. Some people think that Trump will return to Twitter now. Musk says that freedom of speech must be on Twitter. This idea means that anyone can say anything. Musk buys Twitter for 44 billion dollars. 33.5 billion dollars are Musk’s own money. Difficult words: private (something that only belongs to one person or a group of people), ban (to officially stop something), previous (something that exists before). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Autographs are greatly desired celebrity collectibles and lucrative opportunities for actors, musicians and athletes. Celebrity autographs online range from 20 to 200,000 dollars, depending on the signature, especially for deceased artists like Jimi Hendrix and Freddie Mercury. However, in the digital age, fans want something less tangible and more personal, such as selfies and videos to share on social media. Company Cameo created the idea that the selfie is the new autograph. On its platform, fans buy custom videos instead of autographs from over 50,000 celebrities. Prices depend on the popularity and demand for certain artists, and people buy 85% of cameos for holidays or birthdays. The personal aspect of a cameo or a selfie shows that they are completely yours and you can’t sell them to someone else, unlike an autograph. Difficult words: lucrative (something that makes a large profit), tangible (things that can be shown, touched, or experienced), cameo (a short video played by a known actor or celebrity). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Many fans want to have something that connects them with a famous person who they like. Autographs are the most popular things to collect, and they can cost from 20 to 200,000 dollars. Fans can buy autographs online, and the price depends on the popularity of the actor, musician, or athlete. The business is good for celebrities, but more fans now want something personal to share on social media. A US company sells custom videos from more than 50,000 celebrities. Similar to autographs, the price depends on how popular the celebrity is. More than 85% of customers buy cameos as a gift for birthdays or holidays. The difference with a cameo is that the celebrity speaks directly to the person. The video is unique , and it is impossible to sell it to anyone. Difficult words: custom (when someone makes a product exactly as someone orders it), cameo (a short video by a celebrity), unique (one of its kind). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many fans want to have something that reminds them of their favorite actor, singer, or athlete. As times change, fans want different things. Autographs are still the most popular things for fans. They can cost between 20 to 200,000 dollars. It depends on how famous the person is. It can be a very good business for famous people. These days, fans prefer something personal. They want to share it on social media. Autographs are less interesting for young people. People now can buy a short video with a celebrity . The short video is called a cameo. The celebrity speaks only to the person who buys the video. It is not possible to sell the video. On one website, people can choose videos from more than 50,000 celebrities. Difficult words: remind (to make someone remember something), autograph (when a famous person writes his name on a photo, piece of clothes, or other things, and gives or sells it to somebody), celebrity (a famous person, usually in film, music, or sport). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Indonesia is the world’s top palm oil producer; it announced plans to ban exports of the most widely used vegetable oil. Indonesia sells more than half of the global palm oil supply. Indonesia’s president Joko Widodo said that he wanted to ensure the availability of food products in his country, after global food inflation reached a record high. Global prices of crude palm oil reached a historic high this year due to rising demand and weak sales from producers. Additionally, since 2018, Indonesia has stopped allowing new permits for palm oil plantation. Organizations are blamed for deforestation and destroying the habitats of endangered animals, such as orangutans. Russia’s invasion of Ukraine could also raise the cost of packaged food globally, as Ukraine is a major crop grower. It could force governments to choose between vegetable oils in food or biofuel . Difficult words: inflation (a decrease in the purchasing power of money), crude (raw), biofuel (a fuel that comes from plants or animal waste). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Indonesia is the biggest producer of palm oil in the world, and it provides half of the world’s supply . Indonesians use palm oil for cooking, but due to a worldwide increase of food prices, palm oil is becoming more expensive. The country decided to ban the export of palm oil, and experts said that this action would likely increase global prices. Indonesia’s president said that he wanted to make sure that people in his own country had enough food. Also, in 2018, Indonesia made it impossible to make new palm oil farms. This law was an important step, as palm oil farms destroyed forests and many animals died. Difficult words: producer (a person or company who makes things), supply (to make something available), export (to sell products to another country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Palm oil is the most common vegetable oil. The biggest maker of palm oil in the world is Indonesia. It makes half of all palm oil in the world. Indonesian people use the oil for cooking. People cut down trees to grow oil palms. Many animals die, for example, orangutans. Indonesia makes no new plantations since 2018. Now, the country wants to stop the export of palm oil. Everything is more expensive. The war in Ukraine makes the situation even more serious. The price and demand for palm oil is very high. Understandably, Indonesia wants to have enough food for its own people. Difficult words: plantation (a large farm where people grow plants like sugar, coffee, or palm trees), export (an action when people or companies sell things to other countries), demand (how much people want to buy or have the same thing) You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Demonstrators took to the streets in Paris and Lyon to protest against French president Emmanuel Macron’s election win over his far-right rival Marine Le Pen. Violent clashes between protestors happened in the French capital. They had gathered in Place de la République Square, and police responded with firing tear gas to disperse the crowds. In the city of Lyon, protesters threw fireworks at police cars. Macron’s supporters celebrated at the Eiffel Tower, while Le Pen’s supporters reacted in dismay . The French leader became the first person to be re-elected in 20 years. Macron defeated Le Pen in a run-off vote, and he won a second five-year term that prevented him from a major political changes. Although Macron won by a comfortable margin, the abstention rate was the highest since 1969, since a large number of voters were unwilling to vote for either candidate. Difficult words: dismay (a feeling of shock and unhappiness), run-off (a final election, race, or contest), abstention (not voting in favor or against someone or something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

French president Emanuel Macron won over his rival Marie Le Pen, and he became the first leader to be re-elected after 20 years. Macron earned 58.5% of Sunday’s vote, but a very large number of people didn’t vote, since they were unhappy with both candidates . The number was the highest since 1969 for people who didn’t win. If Macron didn’t win, he would be in a very difficult situation with his party. After people saw the results, protests started in the cities of Paris and Lyon. Le Pen’s supporters fought with police, who fired tear gas at them. Macron’s supporters celebrated at the Eiffel Tower, as their candidate would be the president for five more years. Difficult words: rival (a person who competes with somebody else), re-elect (to vote for a politician who then wins, and he can continue in his position), candidate (a person who competes to get a job). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

French president Emanuel Macron wins in a presidential election on Sunday. He defeats Marie Le Pen. Macron becomes the first president who wins again after 20 years. Many people vote for him. Also, many people don’t vote. The number of people who don’t vote is high. It is the highest since 1969. These people are not happy with either candidate . People celebrate who like Macron. People are very unhappy who vote for Le Pen. People protest in the cities of Paris and Lyon. Protesters attack police officers. Macron wins but his situation isn’t easy. Many people want a change in politics. Difficult words: presidential election (the time when people vote for a president), defeat (to win over somebody), candidate (one of the persons who compete to get a job). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last Friday, Bosnia experienced a strong earthquake with magnitude of 5.7. People felt the earthquake throughout the country and in neighboring Croatia, Serbia, and Montenegro. The earthquake hit 42 kilometers southeast of the city of Mostar, and according to scientists, it was at a depth of five kilometers. One person died, at least two were injured, and hundreds of people fled from their homes. The earthquake caused significant damage across several cities, including Ljubinje and Čapljina. People felt it as far as Belgrade, more than 400 kilometers from the epicenter . Scientists warned that aftershocks were likely to happen in the coming days, and they added that the Balkans was prone to seismic activity, so earthquakes were frequent in the area. Difficult words: epicenter (the point on the earth’s surface directly above the origin of an earthquake), aftershock (a smaller earthquake that follows a large earthquake), prone (likely to suffer from something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last week, a strong earthquake hit Bosnia, and it had magnitude of 5.7. People in neighboring Croatia, Serbia, and Montenegro felt the earthquake, too. The earthquake hit the southern part of Bosnia, and its epicenter was about 40 kilometers away from Mostar. People felt it as far away as 400 kilometers in the cities of Belgrade and Ljubinje. Scientists said that it was five kilometers deep underground. In Mostar, one woman died, and two people were injured. The earthquake also caused damage to buildings and roads. Scientists said that earthquakes were common in the area, and they expected that smaller earthquakes would happen in the coming days. Difficult words: magnitude (a number which shows how strong an earthquake is), epicenter (the point on the earth’s surface above an earthquake), common (something that happens often). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A strong earthquake hits Bosnia last week. Its magnitude is 5.7. A magnitude is a number which shows how strong an earthquake is. The strongest earthquake is a number 10. The epicenter is about 40 kilometers away from Mostar. It takes place five kilometers underground. People feel it in cities as far as 400 kilometers away. People in Croatia, Serbia and Montenegro feel it, too. One person dies and two people are hurt. The earthquake breaks houses and roads. Earthquakes happen often in this area. In the next days, scientists expect that smaller earthquakes will happen. Difficult words: earthquake (an event when the ground moves , and it breaks houses and roads), epicenter (the point on the earth’s ground over an earthquake), expect (to think that something will happen). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Grand Slam’s organizers said that it wouldn’t allow tennis players from Russia and Belarus to compete at this year’s Wimbledon due to Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. The organizers stated that in the circumstances of unjustified and unprecedented military aggression, it would be unacceptable for the Russian regime to derive any benefits from the Championships. As a result, Daniel Medvedev won’t be able to compete on the famous grass courts. He is the men’s world number two, Russian, and the reigning champion of the US Open. Along with Medvedev, the men’s world number eight, Andrey Rublev, will miss out, as well as women’s world number four Aryna Sabalenka and two times Grand Slam champion Victoria Azarenka of Belarus. Wimbledon banned athletes after World War II for players from Germany and Japan. Difficult words: unprecedented (never done or known before), regime (a system of government), derive (to get something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On Wednesday, Wimbledon organizers announced that Russian and Belarusian tennis players couldn’t play at this year’s event. The organizers said that there was no reason for Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, and Russia couldn’t get any benefits from the players taking part at Wimbledon. It was the first time in a long time that the organizers banned players. The last time this happened was after World War II for German and Japanese players. This decision affected Daniel Medvedev, the Russian US Open champion and current men’s world number two. Other affected players were the men’s world number eight Andrey Rublev of Russia, the women’s number four Aryna Sabalenka, and number sixteen Victoria Azarenka, both of Belarus. Difficult words: invasion (when a country enters and takes control of another country by force), benefit (something that helps or makes a situation better), decision (what someone does after thinking and talking about what is the best thing to do). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Wimbledon is a tennis competition . It takes place in London, UK. It is two weeks long. Russian and Belarusian tennis players can’t be at Wimbledon this year. Wimbledon organizers say that Russia cannot benefit from the event. Russia attacks Ukraine two months ago. They say there is no reason for the attack. Many sporting events ban Russian and Belarusian athletes. Daniel Medvedev is the second best tennis player in the world. He is Russian. He can’t play at Wimbledon. Other tennis players also can’t play. They are Andrey Rublev of Russia and Aryna Sabalenka and Victoria Azarenka of Belarus. Difficult words: competition (an event in which someone tries to win or be better than the others), benefit (to get help or something good from a situation), ban (to officially stop something from happening). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Parks, a two-year-old Labrador retriever, is the first facility dog for the Orlando Health Hospital for Children. The dog’s now part of the team, and he’s already making a big difference. Parks knows dozens of commands to help calm patients and perform tasks, and he’s learning even more. He brightens the days, and also aids and rehabs when he holds a bat, hits a ball, and plays with children. According to medical workers, Parks adds some more care that they can’t provide. Canine Companions has 475 active facility dog teams, and 70 of them now work in a hospital setting. The organization provides service and facility dogs at no cost. The pups are very eager to work and please, and they’re very smart. They undergo extensive training, and they learn tasks to help people, for example, pulling wheelchairs, picking up dropped items or opening doors. Difficult words: facility dog (a professionally trained dog that does specific tasks), rehab (to return to a normal state after being ill or injured), eager (a strong desire or interest in something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Canine Companions is an organization which trains pups to become facility dogs . The organization has 475 dogs at the moment, and 70 of them work in hospitals. Parks is a two-year-old Labrador retriever, and he’s the first facility dog in a children’s hospital in Orlando, US. According to the staff , Parks is making a big difference. He can help patients when he opens the door or picks up things. He also helps children rehabilitate , and he makes them happy in a way that people can’t. The pups enjoy helping people, and they love learning new things. It takes two months to train them to become facility dogs, and a growing number of hospitals use them. Difficult words: facility dog (a trained dog that does specific tasks for people), staff (all the people who work for a company or organization), rehabilitate (to return to a normal life after an injury or operation). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Canine Companions is an organization which trains pups . The training is two months long. The pups become facility dogs. A facility dog can do special tasks . Such dogs help in hospitals. Or they help people with tasks. The dogs can open doors or pick up things. The organization has 475 dogs. 70 of them work in hospitals. More and more hospitals want to have these dogs. Parks is a two-year-old dog. He works in a children’s hospital in Orlando, US. He does normal things. He also makes children feel better in a way which people can’t. He is very excited to help and learn new things. Difficult words: pup (a young dog), task (work which somebody must do), excited (very happy). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

American actor Johny Depp testified in his 50-million-dollar defamation trial; it was against his ex-wife Amber Heard and he said he never struck her. The lawsuit’s over an opinion article Heard wrote for the Washington Post six years ago; she called herself a victim of domestic violence. Depp denies any abuse; however, Heard’s lawyers presented Depp as abusive and on drug and alcohol binges . Depp’s lawyers presented the domestic violence as a hoax to ruin Depp’s reputation. In a Virginia courtroom, Depp said that it was a complete shock when Heard said that he was violent. The actor also described how people’s attitudes towards him changed after the newspaper published Heard’s op-ed . Difficult words: defamation (an action to damage someone’s good reputation), binge (a time of excessive eating, drinking, or taking drugs), op-ed (a newspaper article that expresses a personal opinion). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Amber Heard was a wife of American actor Johny Depp. Six years ago, she wrote for the Washington Post that Depp abused her, which completely changed the couple’s lives. Last week, a 50-million-dollar trial started in Virginia, and Depp spoke that he never hit his ex-wife or anyone. He said that Heard only wanted to damage his reputation , which already happened, since people behaved differently towards him. Heard’s lawyers said that the actor liked drugs and alcohol, and he often drank or did drugs too much. Depp’s lawyers said that Heard accused Depp of domestic violence only because she wanted to get money from him, to become more popular, and to damage his reputation as an actor. Difficult words: reputation (people’s opinion about someone or something), accuse (to formally say that someone did something wrong), domestic violence (violent behavior at home). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Johny Depp is an American actor. He is very popular. In the past, his wife is Amber Heard. Six years ago, Heard writes for the Washington Post. She writes that Depp abuses her. She says that Depp likes drugs and alcohol. Depp sometimes drinks too much. Also, he hits her. A trial starts last week in Virginia. The trial costs about 50 million dollars. Depp’s lawyers say that Heard wants to hurt his good reputation . Depp speaks in court last week. He says that he never hits his ex-wife or anyone. He says that some people behave differently to him. He says that Heard only wants money and to be more popular. Difficult words: abuse (to behave very badly towards someone), trial (a court event to decide if someone something bad), reputation (what people think about someone or something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Palaeontologists identified a prehistoric species after excavating bones buried on the site of an ancient lake in southern Portugal. They found a giant killer salamander officially known as Metoposaurus algarvensis. It is a distant relative of salamanders living today, and it was wiped out during a mass extinction 201 million years ago, which was long before the death of the dinosaurs. The creature was as long as a small car and had hundreds of sharp teeth in its large and flat head. The animal lived in lakes and rivers during the late Triassic period, living much like crocodiles today and feeding mainly on fish. Difficult words: palaeontologist (a person who does palaeontology – the science of fossilised animals and plants), species (an animal kind), excavate (dig out). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Scientists found bones of a prehistoric animal in southern Portugal. The animal lived in lakes and rivers 200 million years ago – during the Late Triassic period. This animal is the giant killer salamander, officially known as Metoposaurus algarvensis. It was as long as a small car. The salamander was a dangerous predator which fed mainly on fish. It had a large flat head with hundreds of sharp teeth. The amphibian is a distant relative of today’s salamanders. Difficult words: prehistoric (that lived a very long time ago), predator (an animal which eats other animals), amphibian (an animal which lives partly on land and partly in the water). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is about an animal. It lived 200 million years ago. It lived in lakes and rivers. It looked like a crocodile. The animal is called the “giant killer salamander”. It was as long as a small car. It had a large head. Its mouth was full of teeth. It ate fish. People find bones from this animal. They find them in Portugal. Experts study the bones. Difficult words: was (past of “is”), had (past of “have”), ate (past of “eat”). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Over 20 years ago, a seemingly ordinary British couple faked a canoeing accident, and they defrauded hundreds of thousands of pounds from a life insurance policy. John Darwin ran a business renting bed-sits across Durham County until 2000, when he ran into debt and he nearly went bankrupt. Two years later, he went missing while canoeing off Cleveland; however, rescuers were puzzled, as the sea was unusually calm. Darwin’s wife received the death certificate, and she received 250,000 pounds in life insurance. For five years, she lied to the couple’s two sons, while Darwin secretly lived in a bed-sit next door. The couple eventually decided to start a new life in Panama City; however, in 2007, Darwin walked into a London police station, and he claimed he had no memory of the past five years. Police already suspected that the man might be alive and using a false identity. The couple were both jailed for six years for the fraud , and their story became the subject of a TV drama called ‘The thief, his wife and the canoe’. Difficult words: defraud (to illegally get money by saying or doing something dishonest), bed-sit (a one-room apartment), fraud (the crime of getting money by a trick or lying). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

More than 20 years ago, a British couple faked a canoeing accident to get money from life insurance . John Darwin ran a business, but he started to have problems with paying his debts . Two years later, he went missing while he was canoeing. Rescuers were surprised because there was no storm at that time. Darwin’s wife got 250,000 pounds from her husband’s life insurance. Actually, Darwin wasn’t dead, and for five years, he lived in a house next door. Even his two sons thought that the man was dead. In 2007, he walked into a police station in London, and he said that he didn’t remember the past five years. He used a false identity , but police already thought that something was wrong. The couple went to prison for six years. Later, Darwin said that he did the crime, as he thought it was better for his family if he was dead. Difficult words: life insurance (money which someone pays so that if he has an accident or dies, he or his family gets more money from the company), debt (money which somebody owes), false identity (when someone pretends to be someone else). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

John Darwin is a British man. He runs a business. He rents small flats or apartments. Then, he starts to have money problems. He doesn’t know what to do. Darwin goes canoeing 20 years ago. He goes missing . Rescuers are surprised. There is no storm at sea. Darwin’s wife gets 250,000 pounds from her husband’s life insurance . Actually, the man is not dead. He lives in a house next door. Even his two sons think that he is dead. One day, the man comes to a police station. He says that he doesn’t remember the past five years. He uses another name. Police don’t believe him. Darwin and his wife go to prison for six years. Darwin says that he fakes the accident. He says it is better for the family when he is dead. Difficult words: go missing (to be lost and nobody knows you he are), life insurance (money which someone pays so he or his family get more money if he has an accident or he dies), fake (to make something look real but it isn’t). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Sri Lanka’s president Gotabaya Rajapaksa told his new cabinet that he would seek solutions to his country’s problems. The leader appointed the cabinet despite calls for him to resign over an economic crisis, and he said the problem was an opportunity for change. The crisis was partially from a shortage of foreign money and the country’s inability to pay for imports of staple food and fuel. This led to serious food shortages and medicine and very high prices. Large protests began in early April, and people called for the president to resign. Rajapaksa’s cabinet resigned; however, the president refused. He said that the crisis was an opportunity to discuss the views of various political parties that required changes in the constitution and to approve the necessary amendments . Difficult words: cabinet (the government employees that help a president) staple food (the basic and most important food in people’s everyday lives), amendment (a law or change that’s added to the constitution). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Sri Lanka is experiencing a serious economic crisis. The country couldn’t pay for imported food and fuel, which meant that some people had little food and medicine. In early April, big protests started, and people wanted the government to quit. The president’s cabinet quit, but the president refused. Last week, he started a new cabinet, and he said that the crisis was a good chance to make changes in the country. President Gotabaya Rajapaksa said that he was ready to talk to other political groups and discuss their ideas. He also said that it was necessary to make changes in the constitution . Difficult words: imported (things which a country brings from another country and sells them), cabinet (the people who work for the president), constitution (the basic laws of a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Sri Lanka has big problems. The country can’t pay for things from other countries. People don’t have enough food, medicine and fuel . Prices are getting high. People are angry. They start to protest. They ask the government to resign . The government resigns. The president doesn’t want to do it. He chooses a new government. He says that the problems can bring big changes. The president wants to speak with all politicians. Their ideas are important. It is also necessary to change the constitution. The constitution has the basic laws of a country. Difficult words: medicine (drugs which people take when they are ill), fuel (the thing which cars or machines need for power), resign (to leave a job or office). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Japanese researchers developed computerized chopsticks that use an electrical stimulation waveform to enhance the taste of food. Researchers tested the chopsticks on people who follow a low-sodium diet. Japanese people tend to eat a large amount of salt in their diet; however, to prevent severe lifestyle diseases, the amount needs to lower. If people try to avoid salt, they need to avoid their favorite foods, or they need to eat flavorless food. The chopsticks are connected to a device on the eater’s wrist. A weak electric current moves sodium ions and pulls them in the food. Then the eater’s tongue feels the salty taste enhanced by up to one and a half times. Difficult words: electrical stimulation waveform (energy that comes out in small regular amounts), enhance (to improve the quality, amount, or strength of something), sodium ion (a chemical that’s necessary in small amounts for some living things). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Japanese scientists made smart chopsticks . These chopsticks are connected to a special device on a person’s wrist. The device has a small computer to make the chopsticks move while a person eats. Then, sodium ions in the food start to move, and they make the food taste more salty. Scientists tested the chopsticks on people who were on a diet, and they couldn’t eat much sodium . These people were happy, as the food tasted saltier and better. They didn’t need to eat food with no taste. Japanese people eat a lot of salt in their diet, which is bad for a healthy lifestyle. Smart chopsticks could help people who like salty food, but they want to be healthy. Difficult words: chopsticks (a pair of sticks which people in Asia use to eat food), sodium ion (a chemical which is important for some living things), sodium (a soft silver-white chemical which is a part of salt). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Chopsticks are two sticks which people in Asia use to eat food. Usually they are made from wood . Japanese scientists make smart chopsticks. You put a special device on your wrist . The device has a small computer inside. This device connects to the sticks. The sticks move when you eat. Then, the food tastes more salty. The sodium ions in food start to move. Scientists say that the chopsticks are good for people who can’t eat too much salt. Japanese people eat a lot of salt. They don’t like food without salt. Too much salt isn’t good for the body. The chopsticks can help solve this problem. Difficult words: wood (hard material which comes from trees), wrist (the part of the body between the hand and the forearm), sodium ion (a chemical element which is in salt). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Fuentes de Andalucia, a peaceful village in southern Spain, renamed itself ‘Ukraine’ for the duration of Holy Week. On a sign at a roundabout at the village’s entrance, Ukraine and its blue and yellow flag replaced the name of the village. Streets have been renamed City of Kyiv, Odesa, and Mariupol, in the village of more than 7,100 inhabitants which is more than 4,000 kilometers away from Ukraine. The main objective was to raise awareness about the conflict in Ukraine and also about other current wars in the world. Another objective was to support a center for refugee families to host 20 to 25 people and to offer homes. The village raised 3,500 euros within two days towards the planned center. Difficult words: objective (a goal), awareness (the knowledge that something exists), refugee (a person who left his country to escape a war or natural disaster). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Fuentes de Andalucia is a small village of about 7,100 inhabitants , which lies in southern Spain and east of Seville. Last week, the village changed its name to ‘Ukraine’, and it will keep the name over Easter. Officials also changed the names of some streets, and the new names were City of Kyiv, Odesa, and Mariupol. The main reason was to make people aware of the war in Ukraine more than 4,000 kilometers away. The village also wanted to show solidarity with the Ukrainian people. The village raised 3,500 euros in two days, and it plans to build a center for people who are running from the war. Up to 25 people or six families could stay there. Difficult words: inhabitant (a person who lives in a place), aware (when a person knows about something), solidarity (when people help and care about each other). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last week, a village in southern Spain changes its name. The old name of the village is Fuentes de Andalucia. The new name is Ukraine. The village will keep the new name during Easter . Officials also change the names of some streets. The streets have names of Ukrainian cities. Officials want to make people aware about the war in Ukraine. The village is about 4,000 kilometers from Ukraine. 7,100 people live there. They want to help. They raise money for a special center for the Ukrainian people. They raise 3,500 euros in two days. Up to 25 Ukrainian people can stay in the center. Difficult words: Easter (a Christian festival which people celebrate in spring), aware (when a person knows about something), raise (to get money for something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Astrology and forms of divination such as palm reading, tarot cards, or numerology have long influenced Thai culture. However, due to social distancing rules, many fortune tellers are now online to continue their work. Young Thais are experiencing soaring levels of stress from the health crisis and job concerns, and many are getting help from fortune telling. According to health experts, stress levels are very high. A new fortune telling application brings together 7,000 online fortune tellers to people; it has had a sharp increase in the number of users. According to some fortune tellers, since the pandemic, people are asking more questions about careers instead of love and relationships. Difficult words: divination (the skill of saying or discovering what will happen in the future), numerology (the study of numbers, such as a person’s date of birth, in the belief that they have a special meaning in a person’s life), fortune teller (a person who is able to predict a person’s future). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Many Thai people believe in astrology , and they like to know what will happen in their future. They often ask fortune tellers to tell the future. For example, they read tarot cards or use numerology . Since the pandemic, many young Thais have more problems. They worry more about their work, and experts say that the situation is very serious. More people are using fortune tellers’ services because they believe that they will help them feel better. People could not meet during the pandemic, so many fortune tellers worked online. One company employs 7,000 fortune tellers who meet people online. Fortune tellers say that people more often ask about work instead of love and relationships. Difficult words: astrology (the study of the planets and stars’ movements and how they impact people), tarot cards (cards with pictures which some people use to tell the future), numerology (the study of numbers and what they mean in a person’s life). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A fortune teller is a person who predicts someone’s future. He uses different ways to do it. He can use numerology to study numbers and what they mean in someone’s life. He can also use tarot cards or palm reading . Many people go to fortune tellers in Thailand. They like to know what will happen in the future. Many fortune tellers start to work online during Covid-19. More than 7,000 fortune tellers work for one online company. They use a special app to speak to people. Young Thais have more problems with their work. They often speak to fortune tellers. They ask about work. It is different. They often ask about love in the past. Difficult words: predict (to say what will probably happen in the future), tarot cards (cards with pictures which fortune tellers use to talk about the future), palm reading (when a person looks at someone’s hand and its lines, and he says what will probably happen to this person in the future). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A man set out for the Pacific Crest Trail, which stretches from the borders of Mexico to Canada. He decided to take a selfie every single mile along the 4,184-kilometre trek . Andy created a time-lapse video from his five-month hike and he is almost unrecognisable towards the end of the video – he had lost 23 kilograms. Sadly, he never finished the trek, as a snow storm stranded him about 418 kilometres from the end. Difficult words: crest (the top of a mountain or a hill), stretch (extend over an area), trek (a journey), stranded (be stuck, unable to continue). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The Pacific Crest Trail runs across the United States. It starts on the border with Mexico and ends on the border with Canada. It is 2,600 miles long (4,184 kilometres) and runs through the mountains of California, Oregon and Washington. A man went on a hike on the trail and took a selfie at every mile (1.6 kilometres). The man from Texas created a video from the pictures that he took. He looks very different at the beginning and at the end of the video – he lost 50 pounds (23 kilograms) in weight. After five months on the trail, 418 kilometres from the end, he had to stop because a snow storm stranded him. Difficult words: crest (the top of a mountain or a hill), trail (a way you walk on in the countryside), stranded (to be stuck, unable to continue). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Pacific Crest Trail is in the USA. It starts on the border with Mexico. It ends on the border with Canada. It is 2,600 miles long (4,184 kilometres). It goes through the mountains of California, Oregon and Washington. A man goes on the trail. He takes a selfie at every mile (1.6 kilometres). He turns the pictures into a video. You can see how he changes. He is a little fat at the beginning of the video. At the end, he is not. He lost 50 pounds (23 kilograms). The man did not finish the trail. He stopped 418 kilometres from the end – there was a snow storm. Difficult words: crest (the top of a mountain or a hill), trail (a way in the countryside), border (an area where two countries meet). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Tuesday morning, ten people were shot and more than 20 injured in a subway shooting in New York City. First, the gunman in a gas mask filled a crowded subway car with thick black smoke from a canister . Then, he fired on passengers. Reportedly, 40 to 50 passengers were in the carriage, and they tried to get through a locked door. The train slowed and reached a station. Police recovered a gun, a hatchet , and detonated and undetonated smoke grenades. They also announced that they were looking for a 62-year-old man, who they believed was connected with the shooting. The attack brought fear and chaos to New York City, and the city’s mayor Eric Adams said that the US needed action at all levels of government and a change in gun laws to stop such gun violence. Difficult words: canister (a container used for storing things like food, chemicals, or gas), hatchet (a small axe), detonated (exploded). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On Tuesday morning, people in New York were traveling by subway when suddenly one of the carriages filled with black smoke. A man in a gas mask had detonated two smoke grenades, and he started to shoot at the passengers. 40 to 50 people were in the carriage, and police said that the man killed ten and injured more than 20 of them. Other passengers tried to get out of the train, but it wasn’t possible until the train stoopped. The man then ran away, and police announced that they were looking for a 62-year-old man, who could be the killer. New York City’s mayor said that it was necessary to change the gun laws and to stop such attacks. The city also announced that it would double the number of police officers in the New York subway. Difficult words: carriage (one separate part of a train which carries people), detonate (to make something explode), mayor (the leader of a city or town). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

It is Tuesday morning. People are traveling to work. An attack happens on a New York City subway . One man has a gas mask on his face. He detonates two smoke grenades . When the grenades explode, the carriage is full of black smoke. The man starts to shoot. He kills ten people. More than 20 people are hurt. Other people want to get out of the train. Sadly, the doors are locked. When the train stops, people start to run away. Police look for the killer. They think that he can be a 62-year-old man. Officials say that it is important to change the gun laws in the US. Similar attacks must stop. Difficult words: subway (an underground train), detonate (to make something explode), smoke grenade (a bomb which produces a lot of smoke when it explodes). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Islamic State is laying improvised explosive devices (IEDs) in northern Iraq, killing people and preventing local farmers from cultivating their land. Asmaa Khalil leads a team of five women who thoroughly clear IEDs from one patch of land at a time. Khalil said that at the beginning, it was scary to work with mines and IEDs. However, after a month or two of training and working in fields, Khalil got some experience, and the work became easier. The team faced other difficulties, too. Iraqi society didn’t accept women working in a military field , and the women had to follow military rules. Therefore, the team couldn’t tell anyone that they were working in the field. Difficult words: improvised (made without preparation or a plan), mine (a type of bomb that explodes when a person or vehicle touches it), field (a flat space of land; a type of work). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Islamic State laid many mines and other bombs in fields in northern Iraq. These bombs are still killing people, and they make it hard for farmers to grow crops . Asmaa Khalil and five other women decided to clear the fields. At first, it was very difficult, and the women were scared of the bombs. They divided a field into several parts, and they cleared the parts one by one. After a month or two, the work became easier because the women learned how to do it well and safely. The women had another problem, too. They had to follow military rules because officials think that this work is military work. The women couldn’t tell anyone what they did because it was unusual for Iraqi women to do this work. Difficult words: mine (a type of bomb which explodes when someone or something touches it), crops (plants which farmers grow and sell), military (the soldiers or the army). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many bombs are in fields in northern Iraq. Islamic State puts the bombs there. These bombs kill people. Farmers can’t grow crops there. It is too dangerous. A group of women clear a field. The women have another problem. They must follow military rules. Officials say that the work is similar to military work. The women can’t tell anyone what they do. It is not usual in Iraq that women work in the military. Difficult words: crops (plants which farmers grow and sell), divide (to put into parts), military (something that is part of the soldiers and army).
